scope: Source observations only; no independent evaluation or medical validation.
source_anchor_normalization: Long s, ligatures, ordinary spacing, line-wrap breaks, and conventional astronomical-glyph names may be normalized; no substantive corrections.

issues.observation: Dariot Abridged introduces this material, but PDF293 explicitly alternates Dariot and Lilly labels. The owned later rules lack local labels.
issues.consequence: A section-level label alone cannot securely identify every later rule's ultimate author; first-person contributions also must be identified as narrated experience rather than source-neutral laws.
issues.disposition: Unlabeled rules remain ambiguous, except the locally attributed many Astrologians and the separately identified first-person passages. No independent Dariot text was consulted.

issues.observation: The above-earth rule gives the right/upper body; the following under-earth OR diurnal-sign rule visibly prints superiour and fore-part.
issues.consequence: Replacing superiour with inferiour would alter the source even if it seems more systemically plausible.
issues.disposition: Retained superiour exactly; original enlarged crop confirms the reading. No repair made.

issues.observation: The under-earth branch is joined by OR to vitiated in a diurnal sign, and the nocturnal clause elides its subject and qualifiers.
issues.consequence: Forcing an AND or carrying every prior condition into the nocturnal branch changes the antecedent.
issues.disposition: Preserved the OR and flagged inheritance of actor, affliction, and under-earth scope.

issues.observation: The aspected feminine planet is in a Feminine Signe or House; no feminine-house definition appears here.
issues.consequence: A modern engine may misclassify the condition or attach the sign/house test to the wrong planet.
issues.disposition: Preserved both actors and the printed sign/house alternative; no definition imported.

issues.observation: Few, middle, and lower degrees map to member regions but have no numerical boundaries; the clauses continue the masculine/above-earth experience rule.
issues.consequence: Ten-degree bins, numerical lower-degree ordering, or independence from the previous antecedent are not established.
issues.disposition: No decans or intervals added; member scope and inherited-condition ambiguity recorded.

issues.observation: The source distinguishes Ascendant/sign/degree, Sun itself, Sun's house/sign lord, Moon's dispositor, and Ascendant lord's dispositor; some resulting mind/body allocations resist a simple partition.
issues.consequence: Merging roles or reversing outcomes for conceptual consistency would erase material source differences.
issues.disposition: Each role retained locally; no global reconciliation score or repaired mind/body system supplied.

issues.observation: The phrase lists Sun/Moon dispositors OR Ascendant lord OR two of them at least.
issues.consequence: Neither an unqualified one-of-three nor a two-of-three interpretation is secure; coincident physical planets also raise a role-count issue.
issues.disposition: Retained raw alternatives and explicit unresolved minimum/counting semantics.

issues.observation: The original enlarged image reads Jupiter and never oppresseth the Minde but the Body.
issues.consequence: Replacing Jupiter, dropping never, or transferring all Saturn antecedents would change a conspicuous historical assertion.
issues.disposition: Glyph and polarity retained. Extent of the contrary-hereof antecedent remains unstated.

issues.observation: Two ruler/dispositor roles are followed by multiple affliction alternatives, without a rule for mixed conditions on the two roles.
issues.consequence: An executable representation could require one identical state for both or allow different states; the text does not decide.
issues.disposition: Plural subjects preserved; distribution left unresolved.

issues.observation: The aspect sequence after by a is visibly sextile, square, opposition of Mars.
issues.consequence: Substituting conjunction for the unexpected sextile is not source-grounded.
issues.disposition: Kept sextile; enlarged source crop supports the reading.

issues.observation: A planet in the Ascendant, the Ascendant, or the Moon-house lord may be oppressed in the twelfth; scope of that location phrase is unclear.
issues.consequence: A literal location predicate shared by all subjects can be incoherent, but choosing another attachment without annotation also repairs the text.
issues.disposition: Preserved actor alternatives and raw predicate; no single forced executable parse.

issues.observation: The source compares degrees' affliction against their lords' affliction, then reverses the outcome for the reverse comparison.
issues.consequence: No weighting, aggregation, ties, or probability follows from the prose.
issues.disposition: Both comparative directions retained; no score created.

issues.observation: The debility list contains commas and one OR; and free from Saturn/Mars ill aspects has an omitted subject.
issues.consequence: Both list logic and the subject of freedom would require interpretation.
issues.disposition: Raw condition groups and both uncertainties preserved; no silent choice.

issues.observation: The Sun/Ascendant/hour/twelfth significator clause is compressed; Venus has no repeated affliction condition; Mercury's pronouns shift from planet to represented person.
issues.consequence: Adding a Sun rulership requirement, a Venus affliction requirement, or a clinical personality label would go beyond this witness.
issues.disposition: Usually, explicit versus implied conditions, and person-reference inference retained.

issues.observation: The callback describes birth degrees falling to be degrees of a sign containing a present eclipse/conjunction, with at the time of sickness or near it.
issues.consequence: Exact-degree equality, a whole-sign match, and angular versus temporal nearness are not fully specified.
issues.disposition: Optional nativity dependency and all matching/nearness ambiguities preserved.

issues.observation: The sign of an eclipse/conjunction or the eighth-house sign of the yearly revolution of the World falls in natal angles; threatening evil has uncertain scope.
issues.consequence: The world-revolution eighth house cannot be substituted with the natal, question, or illness eighth house.
issues.disposition: Distinct frames, emphasis on natal Ascendant, and modifier scope retained; outside calculation rules remain dependencies.

issues.observation: The span uses first falling sick OR demand, first taking bed with a physician-judgment fallback, a timing question after expected recovery, and the Ascendant lord's sign at question time.
issues.consequence: Treating every reference as one generic event-time chart would erase distinct instructions and the only explicit fallback hierarchy.
issues.disposition: Time origins kept local. No default substituted for an unavailable or uncertain event time.

issues.observation: The close Moon-Sun rule says not above six degrees AND not yet passed/conjoined; Aries or Leo lessens it. The next sentence says twelve degrees and little danger.
issues.consequence: A distance-only test, a zero-only conjunction test, >=12, 6-to-12 interpolation, or an absolute safe outcome is unsupported.
issues.disposition: Inclusive six, phase condition, mitigated-not-removed outcome, exact twelve wording, and missing direction retained.

issues.observation: The three angles are 45, 90, and 135 degrees from the initial Moon place, near those times, and expressly not chronic but acute.
issues.consequence: Adding 180, every 45-degree multiple, exact event times, or chronic applicability expands the rule.
issues.disposition: Only the three angles and acute-only scope retained; no precise time tolerance supplied.

issues.observation: The later first-person aspect observations do not restate acute/chronic scope or distinguish fixed reference positions from moving aspect endpoints.
issues.consequence: Those choices cannot be silently imported from a modern transit technique. The favorable clause describes pronouncing comfort.
issues.disposition: Endpoint/scope ambiguities and prognostic-act evidence type retained.

issues.observation: The opened parenthesis if he had not power or dominion in the disease is unclosed before I found; the Sun is the nearest referent, but the Ascendant lord remains possible.
issues.consequence: Omitting the exclusion or fixing its actor without a flag changes the condition.
issues.disposition: Preserved NOT(power OR dominion), likely Sun reference, alternate actor possibility, and mental-relief-only outcome.

issues.observation: The author counts degrees distant betwixt the Ascendant lord and a benevolent aspected planet, without explicitly defining the distance operation.
issues.consequence: Raw longitude separation, distance to aspect perfection, and rounding are not interchangeable.
issues.disposition: No numeric algorithm added; the source's ordinarily/day relation and speed/angular certainty qualifiers retained.

issues.observation: Lilly uses discretion and disease quality, withholds an automatic common-sign unit, reports Ancients' alternatives, and asks the reader to mix houses, signs, and Moon factors.
issues.consequence: A single fixed sign/house-to-time conversion with weights or priority is not supplied by the whole argument.
issues.disposition: Ancient mappings retained as sets/reference relations alongside Lilly's contextual qualifications; no conflict-resolution formula created.

issues.observation: The incoming sign must give the Ascendant lord essential dignities; the outcome is recovery OR a perceptible good alteration.
issues.consequence: The text does not require outgoing debility, identify a minimum dignity, or guarantee complete recovery at every ingress.
issues.disposition: All stated qualifiers and the outcome alternative retained; dignity definitions remain external dependencies.

issues.observation: The conditional example is 28 degrees on the sixth cusp AND a common sign, followed by vary in less than two weeks.
issues.consequence: Generalizing to >=28, all late degrees, full recovery, or an observed dated patient would misrepresent the example.
issues.disposition: Recorded as one numerical illustration, with strict upper bound, unspecified direction, and unspecified restated time origin.

issues.observation: Generic remembered experience, usual methods, prognostic statements, and one numeric illustration occur, but no dated enquiry, chart, denominator, or independent endpoint occurs in the owned span.
issues.consequence: Author confidence and claimed absence of remembered failure cannot become validated evidence, trial counts, or accuracy statistics.
issues.disposition: Inventory distinguishes each evidence type; actual dated enquiries, present charts, and independent endpoints each count zero.

issues.observation: The entire upper paragraph promises later practical figures and describes translating/inserting Hermes before the divider; Hermes' own heading and text start below it.
issues.consequence: Stopping before the translation rationale would omit owned material; assigning the preceding records to Hermes or extracting below the divider would cross the boundary.
issues.disposition: Full upper bridge included. Forward examples remain an open dependency; ancient authorship/esteem is reported, not established. Lower Hermes text excluded.
